source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Press load default,save and reboot.
3. Boot in BIOS,compare setting should matches SPEC.
4. Change BIOS all/random setting in this function,to non-default  setting.
5. Save and reboot.
6. Boot in BIOS and check your setting still exist.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. The default setting should matches SPEC."
2. No error log happen.
3. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
4. Check your set still exist.

original_test_intent: Verify TLS Authentication defaults and persistence of approved non-default controls without weakening trust validation, breaking approved HTTPS/PXE boot, introducing an unapproved trust anchor or exposing private authentication material.
original_method: Manually load BIOS defaults, compare named TLS fields with SPEC, apply a bounded trust/authentication matrix, save/reboot, verify persistence and validate the approved certificate chain and service on an isolated network with secret-safe evidence.
manual_activity: An engineer must operate and visually accept TLS firmware controls and any certificate-store workflow. Automated handshake/service logs are supporting evidence only and must exclude secrets.
required_inputs: Board/BIOS/BMC and UEFI TLS implementation identity
Named auth/trust/certificate fields, store semantics and SPEC defaults
Approved bounded values, CA/trust anchors and certificate-chain metadata
Isolated HTTPS/PXE service identity, expected validation results and immutable image if booted
Credential redaction/rotation, independent console/OOB and trust recovery
safety_requirements: Never operationalize all/random or add/remove trust anchors and certificates without exact approval and recovery.
Never collect, display or commit private keys, passwords, tokens or unredacted credential material.
Use only isolated approved services and test certificates; verify server identity, chain, expiry and intended trust before connection.
Do not weaken validation, enable unauthenticated fallback or use a production deployment endpoint.
Stop on secret exposure, unexpected trust success/failure, wrong service/image, boot failure or management loss.
Restore the approved trust state; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect redacted, non-secret certificate metadata, trust-store fingerprints where safely exposed, UEFI boot/network state, isolated service handshake logs and BMC/OS health.
Compare approved expected validation outcomes without importing/exporting private keys or mutating trust.
Do not drive BIOS, manage credentials/certificates, start an unapproved boot/deployment or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve exact fields, trust chain, test service, secret handling, expected validation outcomes and recovery.
Perform and capture default-first and bounded non-default firmware/certificate phases with secrets redacted.
Interpret security/boot evidence and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects agent BIOS execution. No source command exists; OS TLS settings or BMC certificates are different trust domains and are not substitutes.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve the firmware method and add version-recorded, redacted certificate metadata plus isolated service handshake and boot evidence only.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The default-first lifecycle, null script and 5/20-minute fields are retained; all/random remains source text only.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map each firmware control to trust store, validation behavior and approved HTTPS/PXE service; test bounded valid, invalid and recovery scenarios using non-production certificates while recording only public metadata/fingerprints.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact UEFI TLS/HTTPS implementation, network boot stack and project PKI policy.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC/NIC firmware, TLS service/library versions and public certificate fingerprints/validity.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform TLS Auth/HTTPS boot documentation and approved PKI policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces random changes with explicit chain/validation scenarios, secret-safe evidence and isolated service identity.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; preserves defaults/persistence and adds positive/negative validation, provenance and secret-protection coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Field/store semantics, chain, service, expected results, redaction and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A TLS handshake outside firmware cannot prove UEFI validation behavior; firmware-path evidence remains required.

project_override_considerations: A project may select named trust operations and HTTPS/PXE scenarios. Results must list excluded algorithms, stores, chains and boot paths and cannot claim general TLS compliance.
expected_evidence: Platform identity, field/default/store matrix, approved public chain metadata, isolated service and recovery
Baseline redacted trust fingerprints, firmware boot/network values and health
Load Default captures plus SPEC and validation comparison
Non-default captures, persistence and identity-correlated positive/negative service results
Approved final trust state, secret-safe logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The default-first and persistence lifecycle agrees with the criteria. Exact trust stores, certificates and services are project readiness inputs, not contradictory source facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The TLS configuration lifecycle is clear. Missing PKI/service inputs prevents a project run but does not make the master case permanently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees on manual firmware operation and adds trust-domain, service-identity and secret-protection safeguards.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its isolated TLS/boot evidence while correcting classification to MANUAL ONLY.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates firmware acceptance from automated handshake evidence and forbids credential leakage or cross-layer substitution.

review_improvement: Prevents a persisted TLS setting from being accepted when trust validation is weakened, the wrong service is contacted or sensitive material leaks into evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Core acceptance requires interactive firmware configuration and visual certificate/trust handling. Automated TLS telemetry can corroborate outcomes but cannot replace that manual activity, so MANUAL ONLY is required.
no_automatic_retry: Do not automatically repeat trust changes, certificate operations, handshakes or boot attempts after validation, secret, service, boot or management anomalies; preserve first evidence and obtain engineer disposition.
